items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We did a record of that standard tune, Time After Time... And I can’t remember how we played together the first time.

ctx.x: And where, if at all, does that relate to what we’re talking about?

I don’t know. I like the title, though. Instead of Bossa Antigua… I mean, instead of bossa nova, it’s old. I think Paul was bright enough to know that it wasn’t gonna sound like a real South American tune. Boy, Paul was really special, too, as you know. We did a record of that standard tune, Time After Time, and he plays the melody, or whatever on the way out, and he plays something that is so much more beautiful than the original tune. (laughs) I can’t believe it, the way… he just was so melodic and everything,…
We will come back to Paul.
